items.title: Israel’s siege on Gaza is forcing dentists to operate in the streets
items.description: Scarce resources and office space mean that dental work is a luxury for most people in Gaza.

items.title: Why Ukraine’s drained Kakhovka Dam is strategic for Russia
items.description: Small groups of Russian soldiers have been inching forward through the vast, drained Kakhovka reservoir since they blew up the dam in June 2023. Russian forces are infiltrating this “no man’s land” for reconnaissance purposes rather than for a future military offensive, said a military expert.

items.title: Palestinian teens killed during settler attack on West Bank village, officials say
items.description: Al-Mughayyir's council says they were trying to stop settlers stealing sheep, but the Israeli military says they threw stones at its troops.

items.title: US sanctions halt TOEFL and GRE tests in Iran, disrupting study plans
items.description: Students in Iran can no longer take English-language proficiency exams after the suspension of a US sanctions exemption. Applicants say the move threatens university deadlines and adds costly travel obligations.

items.title: Outside forces fuel Sudan war, new report finds
items.description: Foreign recruitment and external support networks are fuelling the brutal conflict in Sudan, independent UN human rights investigators said on Thursday in a new report, calling for accountability as fighting continues between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

items.title: Why Was There A Shoot-Out In Kyiv Between Security and Intelligence Agents?
items.description: An armed clash between Ukraine’s military intelligence and security service left three officers wounded in Kyiv. Both sides gave conflicting accounts, while President Zelenskyy called the incident “absolutely disgraceful.”

items.title: Drone Wall Rises: Ukraine Bets on Its Best Corps
items.description: A two-week roundup of the Russia-Ukraine war: Ukraine's 1st and 3rd Corps take command of the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk defense, Russia launches a major ballistic missile strike on Kyiv, and Ukrainian forces hit a record 21 Russian oil refineries in August. Plus new weapons debuts, a Banderol missile strike on Pechenihy, an…

items.title: U.S.-Israel relations are on the rocks ahead of elections
items.description: Relations between the Trump administration and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have turned rocky since Trump called a truce with Iran. Trump seeks progress in Gaza, but Netanyahu is taking a defiant stance ahead of an election.

items.title: In Cina emissioni di CO2 in calo dell'1% durante la guerra in Iran
items.description: Crollano i consumi di petrolio mentre aumentano i veicoli elettrici

items.title: Ukraine and Russia's asymmetric war of attrition
items.description: Kyiv and Moscow have stepped up attacks on each other's infrastructure in recent weeks, aiming to weaken the opposing economy and undermine morale. Ukraine has paid a heavier price because it does not possess ballistic missiles and finds it increasingly difficult to intercept those targeting its territory.

items.title: As US steps up pressure on Iran, ordinary people say they’re paying the price
items.description: Iran’s economy was in ruins even before the war, and before U.S. President Donald Trump’s latest “D-Day” sanctions. So far, ordinary Iranians are bearing the brunt and feeling apathetic, meaning surviving leaders, for now, might face a lower risk of an uprising.

items.title: Why the Middle East Oil Shock Failed to Save Russia’s Budget
items.description: Six months into the U.S.-Iran war, Russia’s oil windfall looks surprisingly meager despite initial predictions of a revenue boom.
